key_insight: SrLaCoNbO6 shows strong spin-lattice coupling with phonon and local-structure anomalies well above its antiferromagnetic transition, consistent with fluctuating Kitaev-like magnetic correlations.
engineering_relevance: The results highlight how Raman spectroscopy and EXAFS can detect hidden magnetic-structural coupling in ordered double perovskites, informing the design of materials with tunable spin, lattice, and magnetostrictive behavior.
method: Temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy from low temperature to well above TN
Co K-edge EXAFS to probe local bond distances and disorder around Co ions
Analysis of phonon frequency, linewidth, spectral weight, Fano asymmetry, and low-energy continuum
evidence_signal: Anomalies appear around 60 K and 160–180 K in both Raman modes and EXAFS metrics, while a broad excitation-energy-independent continuum supports fluctuating magnetic excitations.
watch_item: The observed anomalies may include a structural contribution, so the magnetic interpretation is suggestive rather than fully exclusive.
paper_title: Raman spectroscopic signature of Kitaev magnetism and complex spin-lattice coupling in S = 1/2 antiferromagnet SrLaCoNbO$_6$ double perovskite
